⚙️ Settings

Appearance, path profiles, system configuration, and external connections.

🔌 External Access

Master switch for everything that reaches outside this machine: the Azure Service Bus event listener, the cloud relay poller, and the mobile / phone command bridge.

When disabled, the server stops polling the relay, disconnects Service Bus, and refuses connect/pair requests. Your local agents, schedules, boards and the browser UI keep working — only the external bridges are severed. Takes effect immediately; no restart.

🔒 External access is not available in this build. Outbound bridges (Service Bus, cloud relay, mobile/phone) are disabled until stronger guardrails ship. Everything local — agents, schedules, boards and the browser UI — works normally.

⛔ External access is currently disabled, so the Service Bus, mobile relay and connection settings are hidden. Enable the switch above to manage them.

Optional inbound channel for external callers. The mobile relay below works without it.

📱 Mobile Relay

The mobile app connects through the Azure relay. Devices are authorized via the Connected Users below (use the 📱 button to pair). Mobile traffic appears in the Live Log, Sessions, and History tabs.

Appearance, path profiles, system configuration, and external connections.

🧭 Experience level

Basic is a simplified single view — Home, Workspaces, Code Flow, Agents and Marketplace — with the features you need and nothing else. Advanced unlocks the full Productivity / Management workspace with every page.

➕ Add features

Switch on extra capabilities while keeping the simplified Basic layout. Each one adds its page to the sidebar.

Every feature is already available in Advanced mode. Switch back to Basic to curate a simpler view.

🚀 Getting started guide

The onboarding guide on Home disappears once its steps are complete or you dismiss it. Replay it any time — this only shows the walkthrough and never changes your agents, tasks, or boards.

🎨 Appearance

Choose how the dashboard looks. "System" follows your operating system setting.

🎨 Color palette

Recolor the whole dashboard. "Follow organization" uses the current org's theme, or the neutral Graphite default when no org is selected.

✨ Icon set

Replace the system menu & panel emoji with a line-icon style. "Emoji (classic)" keeps the original emoji. Your message, chat and code content is never changed.

⬜ Corner rounding

Control how rounded panels, cards and buttons look. Soft is the default. Reduced tightens every corner; Square nearly flattens them. Avatars and status dots always stay round.

🎬 Page transitions

Animate the content area when you move between pages. Fly-in sends the page in from a random side each time; Wipe reveals it left-to-right. Honors your system's reduced-motion setting.

Speed Fast Slow

💬 Chat

Applies to every agent and manager conversation. Both are on by default.

Reasoning & steps shows the model's thinking and tool calls inline. Live updates polls faster while a response streams.

🧠 Models

Pick which Copilot model powers each kind of work. These apply everywhere — manual runs, schedules, triggers, chat and manager orchestration. A per-agent model override (if set on an agent) always wins. Leave a category on Runtime default to use Copilot's default model.

Ad-hoc agent & manager conversations (SPA and mobile).

Scheduled/triggered agent runs, tasks, flow steps and manager sub-agents.

The manager "brain" and flow AI condition/judge evaluators.

🤖 System agents

These are the app's built-in AI agents. You can't rewrite their base prompts, but you can add standing custom instructions (tone, focus, priorities) that are appended to every run, and optionally pin a specific model. Your instructions are subordinate to each agent's required output — they can't break parsing.

⤴ Azure DevOps defaults

A shared Azure DevOps org & project used to pre-fill both the Export to AzDO dialog and the New dev card dialog — set it once here and you won't have to retype it. You can still override per export or per dev card.

Optionally Connect to preselect a repository & branch for Export — the New dev card dialog lists repositories itself when you open it.

✅ Saved.

👥 Code Flow reviewer groups

Groups you belong to (Azure DevOps groups / GitHub teams), e.g. Dotnet-Core-Engineering. When a pull request lists one of these groups as a reviewer, Code Flow surfaces it under Active PRs (reviews needed) alongside PRs where you're a direct reviewer. Matched by the group's display name (case-insensitive), exactly as it appears on the PR. GitHub and Azure DevOps are managed separately since group names rarely match across the two.

Azure DevOps groups

GitHub teams

Note: GitHub only exposes team review-requests on the PR when the team is still awaiting review; once anyone on the team reviews, GitHub drops the team from the PR.

No groups yet — only PRs where you're a direct reviewer surface under reviews.

☁️ Cloud Sync

Each machine backs up its own agents, managers, tasks and event config to its own cloud namespace. Every machine runs its own schedules and responds to its own events independently.

Your config syncs automatically to this machine's own namespace. To borrow agents from another machine, use Browse Other Machines.

Advanced — manual sync

Sync happens automatically. Push forces an immediate backup of this machine's config to the cloud. Restore overwrites this machine's local config from its own latest cloud backup — use only for disaster recovery.

🖥️ Connected Machines

All machines running this app and sharing this cloud config. Each runs its own schedules and events; your mobile device chooses which one to listen to.

🧰 Browse Other Machines

Each machine keeps its own agents and managers in the cloud. Install any of them into this machine's namespace to reuse them here.

📦 Dependencies

The bundled copy is the floor; the app keeps an updatable copy that actually runs. Updates are staged, validated, then swapped in atomically — a failed update never breaks what you have. Everything here is per-user; no admin rights required.

Default channel

Data location

Where TheOffice.AI stores your settings, boards, agents, managers and run history. Move it to OneDrive or another folder to keep it synced and preserved across upgrades. A small breadcrumb file stays at the default location so the app can always find your data.

Worktree location

Root folder where all new worktrees are created — both dev-card and PR-review worktrees. A short root avoids Windows MAX_PATH (260-char) errors on deeply-nested repos.

Leave blank for a short auto path. Existing worktrees keep their location — only newly-created ones use this root.
